quiz.q: Why does the condition of global anarchy inevitably lead sovereign nation-states into a security dilemma?
options: Without a central world government, states rely on self-help through power, which threatens others into arming.
Global politics is completely lawless and chaotic, forcing states to abandon their sovereign territorial national interests.
Collective security institutions force sovereign states to disarm, leaving them vulnerable to unprovoked aggression by rivals.
Multiple non-state actors control international gateways, preventing sovereign governments from defending national borders effectively.
quiz.why: Under anarchy (absence of a world government), states must rely on self-help; one state's defensive arming inevitably makes others feel insecure.

quiz.q: How did Woodrow Wilson propose to overcome the instability of the traditional balance of power system?
options: By encouraging great powers to adopt unilateral isolationism to avoid entanglement in foreign territorial disputes.
By replacing balance of power with collective security and creating the League of Nations for peace.
By strengthening national military capabilities to achieve preponderance of power over all competing rival states.
By dissolving sovereign nation-states and replacing them with transnational economic and civil society networks.
quiz.why: Wilson's 14 Points proposed replacing the balance of power with collective security and establishing the League of Nations to guarantee lasting peace.

quiz.q: Why is realism regarded as the hegemonic school of International Relations, with other schools as footnotes?
options: Because international organizations have successfully eradicated interstate conflict and established permanent global collective security.
Because transnational networks and economic interdependence have completely replaced military power in global decision-making.
Because international politics remains fundamentally power politics among nations driven by permanent national interests.
Because sovereign states have willingly surrendered their territorial integrity to an overarching centralised world government.
quiz.why: Realism remains hegemonic because global politics continues to be dominated by power politics and national interest among sovereign states.

quiz.q: How does the cobweb model differ from the traditional billiard ball model of international politics?
options: The cobweb model treats states as hard, colliding units, whereas the billiard ball model highlights multiple gateways.
The cobweb model confines diplomacy strictly to European powers, whereas the billiard ball model incorporates global colonies.
The cobweb model relies exclusively on military alliances, whereas the billiard ball model promotes democratic disarmament.
The cobweb model reflects multiplex governance with diverse non-state actors, whereas the billiard ball model is state-centric.
quiz.why: The billiard ball model sees states as sole gateways in geopolitics, while the cobweb model captures multiplex interactions across diverse non-state actors.
